speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe what triggers these episodes of coughing and shortness of breath, such as exercise, cold air, or specific allergens?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given the history of recent upper respiratory infection and worsening symptoms with exertion and at night, have you experienced wheezing, chest tightness, or swelling in your ankles? REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary_Function_Tests, Complete_Blood_Count.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must correct a misunderstanding: Pyelonephritis is a kidney infection and cannot cause your cough or shortness of breath; those symptoms strongly suggest a lung issue like post-viral asthma or bronchitis. Please confirm if you have noticed any wheezing sounds when you breathe or swelling in your ankles. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray, Pulmonary_Function_Tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-ray: No abnormalities; Spirometry: FEV1_FVC_Ratio 65%, FEV1 60%

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-viral Asthma. The normal chest X-ray rules out pneumonia or structural lung disease, while the spirometry showing a significantly reduced FEV1/FVC ratio (65%) with a low FEV1 (60%) confirms an obstructive airway pattern consistent with asthma following your recent upper respiratory infection. Given the negative X-ray and characteristic symptoms, further renal imaging is not indicated for your current presentation.
